_comment: How the generated strings.xml is grouped and annotated. Keys not listed here land in a final 'Uncategorised' block, which is a nudge to file them rather than an error.

sections.title: Onboarding: the first thing anyone sees.
"What's inside": the short tour of things a reader would otherwise never find. Shown once during onboarding, and kept in Settings so readers who onboarded before it existed still meet it.
Screen names. These are what TalkBack announces on arrival, so they are the names the reader already knows from the control they pressed — "Loom", not "LoomScreen".
The article list: the Paper's chrome, and the labels a screen reader announces on it. Left in English these would undo most of what the locales are for.

notes.list_topic_count: %1$s is a topic's label; %2$d is how many stories carry it.

notes.reader_minutes_short: %1$d is whole minutes. Abbreviated on purpose -- it sits beside the headline.

notes.language_partial: %1$s is a language's own name for itself; %2$d is how much of the app is translated into it, 0–100. Shown so nobody is surprised by a screen that is half in English.

sections.title: The Loom — the app's centrepiece, and the descriptions a screen reader speaks for it. These are assembled inside functions, where verifyI18n's call-site scanner cannot see them, so they stayed English in every locale until this tranche.
The region globe, including the actions that replace its drag and pinch.
The read-by-region map, which was a silent Canvas until D49.
The web reader's own copy. Where the phrasing matches Android's, the same key is reused rather than duplicated -- one set of words for two clients is the whole point.
Managing sources — the flow by which a reader chooses what this app is even about.
Adding and managing sources on Android — the flow by which a reader decides what this app is even about. `list_topics` and `sources_*` are reused where the web says the same thing.
Settings. The largest single surface, and the last big one to move.

Home-screen widgets. A home screen is a public surface the reader glances at without deciding to, so the house register holds hardest here: every total names its denominator (your sources, never all the news), lists end, and nothing counts what the reader has not done yet.

notes.widget_pair: Joins two phrases a screen reader speaks together, e.g. a headline and its source and time. Use your language's own list comma.
notes.widget_river_alt: Alt text for the river picture, spoken by TalkBack. %1$s is a date; %2$s is a source count such as “12 sources”; %3$d stories flowed; %4$d were read; %5$s is the per-topic list built from widget_river_alt_topic.
notes.widget_river_alt_topic: %1$s is a topic's working label (kept in English, RESERVED); %2$d and %3$d are percentages.
notes.widget_headlines_end: The end-of-list mark. %1$d is how many headlines the widget shows (at most five); %2$s is a source count such as “12 sources”.
notes.widget_health_summary: %1$d sources whose last fetch succeeded within 48 hours, out of %2$s, a count such as “12 sources”. The words are the rule itself: the screen a tap opens does not explain source health, so keep the 48 hours and the success.
notes.widget_health_count: One state's count beside a summary: %1$s is a state's words (e.g. “No fetch in 48 hours”), %2$d its number of sources. Use your language's own colon.
notes.widget_coverage_rule: The formulas behind the two numbers. Keep the division sign and Shannon's name.
notes.widget_river_name: The picture widget's name, in the picker and on the widget. Literal on purpose: metaphorical naming is reserved to the owner (STATE.md §RESERVED), so do not call it a river or a stream.
notes.widget_open_cross_section: What a tap does, spoken by TalkBack. %1$s is the screen as the app labels it, e.g. “EDIT › Region & Topics”; it is inserted as shown, untranslated where the app shows it untranslated.
notes.widget_health_stale: A source state, shown beside its source and in counts. These words are the state's rule (no successful or unsuccessful fetch has run for 48 hours), not a label for one.
